title: HOS Commands 0.2 definitions
description: Draft. The definitions HOS Commands 0.2 adds to HOS Core 0.1, which stays unchanged: command types, the command lifecycle, its reason codes, the references a command, an approval and a policy share, and the preconditions a command may carry.

commandType.description: The command types of the first series. Every other type is refused: HOS Commands 0.2 defines controlled requests, not a general privilege to automate.

commandStatus.description: The lifecycle of a command. succeeded, rejected, failed, expired and cancelled are final: a correction is a new command.

commandReason.description: Why a command ended without succeeding. rejected means refused before execution (policy, capability, tenant, approver); failed means approved but not achieved.

commandDigest.description: sha-256: followed by the SHA-256 of the canonical form (RFC 8785) of a command, in lower-case hexadecimal. An approval carries the digest of the command its approver saw: a command changed afterwards no longer matches.

policyRef.description: The version of the policy in force when a command or an approval was evaluated.

evidenceRef.description: A fact or a situation a command rests on: where it comes from and its id.

requesterRef.description: Who asks for a command: user (a staff member) or integration (an application, a future agent, which only proposes), with a pseudonymous, tenant-scoped reference. Never a name or contact detail.

approverRef.description: Who approves a command: always a person, with a pseudonymous reference. An integration never approves.

approverRole.description: A role of the tenant, such as front_office_manager. A policy names the roles that may approve; the approval records the role its approver decided under.

preconditionKind.description: The kinds of precondition a command may carry.

confirmationEventType.description: The event types that confirm a command: the facts of the authoritative system that show the effect.
